etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French adopter, from Latin adoptō; ad +‎ optō (“to choose, desire”), equivalent to ad- +‎ opt.

definitions.definition: To take voluntarily (a child of other parents) to be in the place of, or as, one's own child.
To obtain (a pet) from a shelter or the wild.
To contribute towards the upkeep of (a child or animal), in exchange for occasional stories, pictures, etc.
To take by choice into the scope of one's responsibility.

quote.citation: 2020 December 30, Paul Stephen, “Chirk station is truly blooming”, in Rail, page 49:
quote.text: Sixteen years ago, the station entered into a new chapter when it was adopted by the Friends of Chirk Station (FoCS) volunteer group, under the Arriva Trains Wales Station Adopters programme.

definitions.definition: To take (a child, heir, friend, citizen, etc.) by choice into a relationship.
To take or receive as one's own what is not so naturally.

quote.citation: 2014 November 14, Blake Bailey, “'Tennessee Williams,' by John Lahr [print version: Theatrical victory of art over life, International New York Times, 18 November 2014, p. 13]”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: [S]he [Edwina, mother of Tennessee Williams] was indeed Amanda [Wingfield, character in Williams' play The Glass Menagerie] in the flesh: a doughty chatterbox from Ohio who adopted the manner of a Southern belle and eschewed both drink and sex to the greatest extent possible.

definitions.definition: To select and take or approve.

quote.citation: 1876, Henry Martyn Robert, Robert’s Rules of Order‎[2], Chicago: S.C. Griggs & Co., Article XIV, Section 71, p. 156:
quote.text: Every society should adopt an order of business adapted to its special wants.

quote.citation: 1997, “Buying a Rural Property”, in Back to Basics, Surry Hills, NSW: Reader's Digest (Australia) Pty Limited, page 10:
quote.text: Having found a property that 'feels' right you then have to adopt a hard-headed attitude and consider the realities of life in a new environment.

definitions.definition: (chess, slang) To beat an opponent ten times in a row.

quote.citation: 2018 June 19, Peter Doggers, “(title)”, in Chess.com‎[3], archived from the original on 2022-05-21:
2020 May 27, “Adopt-A-Danny Returns Wednesday With Ian Nepomniachtchi”, in Chess.com‎[4], archived from the original on 2020-05-27:
quote.text: Wednesday's event will offer the Russian grandmaster three opportunities to adopt Rensch, though just like in the Speed Chess Championship, Nepomniachtchi will have to race against the clock.

quote.citation: 2022 April 12, Jacob Sweet, “The Most Popular Chess Streamer on Twitch”, in The New Yorker‎[5], archived from the original on 2022-08-26:
quote.text: "That's it, that's it!" the Grandmaster Eric Hansen bellowed after following nine straight losses with a win. "You are not adopting me! Not today, not today!"

quote.citation: 2022 December 7, Colin McGourty, “Carlsen plays "horribly", beats Gukesh 23:7”, in chess24‎[6], archived from the original on 2022-12-09:
quote.text: There was wasn't much for Gukesh fans to cheer, but at least he avoided the fate of Maghsoodloo, who was "adopted", i.e. beaten 10 games in a row. Gukesh struck in the 2nd 3+1 game, when he was dangerously close to that mark.
